record.paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
record.context_brief: Open WASEP activity-conditioned symmetry breaking beyond mapped range
record.original_question: For an open WASEP with left and right reservoir densities both equal to 1/2, bulk asymmetry p/q = exp(2ν₁/L), and activity bias s = λ/L², determine whether particle-hole symmetry is broken when λ exceeds ν₁²/2, the range not accessible through the real-parameter mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP. Here symmetry breaking means that the optimal density profile for the activity-conditioned large deviation is no longer flat.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the open weakly asymmetric simple exclusion process (WASEP) on the lattice {1, 2, ..., L} defined as follows. Each site is either occupied by a single particle or empty. In the bulk, a particle at site i attempts to jump to site i+1 at rate p and to site i-1 at rate q (jumps are rejected if the target site is occupied), with the weak asymmetry scaling p/q = exp(2ν₁/L) for a fixed real parameter ν₁. At the left boundary, particles are injected at site 1 (when empty) at rate consistent with reservoir density ρ_L = 1/2 and ejected from site 1 at the corresponding rate; the right boundary at site L is coupled analogously to a reservoir of density ρ_R = 1/2.

Let K_t denote the total number of particle jumps (in either direction, summed over all bonds, including the boundary bonds) up to time t — i.e., the dynamical activity. Tilt the path measure by the activity by introducing a bias parameter s = λ/L² with λ ∈ ℝ, weighting trajectories by exp(-s K_t). In the joint limit t → ∞ followed by L → ∞, the typical (most probable) density profile ρ*(x), x ∈ [0,1], conditioned on this activity bias can be characterized via a hydrodynamic large deviation principle.

The model has a particle-hole symmetry: replacing the occupation η_i by 1 - η_i (together with reversing the asymmetry direction) leaves the dynamics with ρ_L = ρ_R = 1/2 invariant. The symmetric flat profile ρ*(x) ≡ 1/2 is always a critical point of the rate functional. One says that particle-hole symmetry is dynamically broken at parameters (ν₁, λ) if the optimal profile ρ*(x) achieving the activity large deviation is non-flat (i.e. ρ*(x) ≢ 1/2).

It is known (via a real-parameter mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP) that for λ ≤ ν₁²/2 the symmetry-breaking question is settled within an explicit parameter range. The problem is:

Determine whether, for λ > ν₁²/2, particle-hole symmetry is broken in the activity-conditioned open WASEP described above — i.e., decide whether the optimal density profile ρ*(x) ceases to be the flat profile 1/2 in this regime, and if so, characterize the transition.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open problem about the activity-conditioned open WASEP with symmetric reservoirs at density 1/2: the standard mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP requires real parameters and only covers λ ≤ ν₁²/2, leaving the regime λ > ν₁²/2 unresolved. A targeted web search did not surface a subsequent publication settling whether particle-hole symmetry is broken in this regime, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: The range λ > ν₁²/2 is not accessible to the mapping (as long as one keeps real values of the parameters), so that we cannot conclude whether particle-hole symmetry is broken or not in this range.
status_evidence.claim: The regime λ > ν₁²/2 lies outside the parameter range covered by the real-parameter mapping, and the symmetry-breaking question there is left unresolved.
